target.title: fix(ui): report WhatsApp logout no-ops
target.body:
Closes #105926

AI-assisted: yes. I understand and reviewed the change.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users logging out of WhatsApp in Settings → Channels would see “Logged out.” and lose the visible QR/connection state when the Gateway reported that no stored session was cleared.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Control UI now consumes the existing `cleared` / `loggedOut` result from `channels.logout`. Confirmed logout clears local login state; a semantic no-op preserves that state, explains the possible causes, and still refreshes channel status.

## User Impact

Users no longer receive false confirmation that WhatsApp credentials were removed. If no session exists or safe credential cleanup is refused, the UI retains useful recovery state and reports the no-op accurately.

## Evidence

- Exact head `1c03f131c595580759dbce906a8d6c20fd231b94`, trusted Testbox `tbx_01kxcspkwndza4h1hz3pn33ssf` (`coral-shrimp-f888`), Actions run `29222635318`: 7/7 focused controller tests passed.
- Same exact head: 1/1 Chromium mocked-Gateway E2E passed, verifying the false result, preserved QR, absence of success text, one logout request, and post-action status refresh.
- Fresh structured autoreview after rebase: clean, no accepted/actionable findings, 0.95 confidence.
- `git diff --check` and targeted `oxfmt --check`: passed.
- `pnpm check:changed` reaches the TypeScript LOC ratchet and fails only on unrelated files already over/stale against the newly landed baseline on current `main`; this patch leaves `ui/src/i18n/locales/en.ts` exactly at its 3,754-line ratchet.
- Real-account destructive proof unavailable because the local Gateway has no WhatsApp plugin. The Gateway result contract and both success/no-op controller branches are covered; the no-op user path is exercised in Chromium.
- No screenshot uploaded because image upload to a public destination was not separately approved; browser assertions provide the UI evidence.
